actions.action: Perform thermography inspections on the inverter to identify hot spots indicating potential failure modes.
actions.expected_impact: Early detection of thermal issues could prevent severe incidents, which account for 21.6% of the equipment cost.

actions.action: Conduct IV-curve tracing and insulation resistance tests on the DC field upstream to detect degradation or short circuits.
actions.expected_impact: Identifying electrical degradation early can reduce the risk of severe incidents, which represent 23.8% of the equipment cost.

actions.action: Implement a regular connector torque check schedule for all DC field connections.
actions.expected_impact: Proper torque maintenance can mitigate connection failures, potentially reducing the recurrence of incidents.

actions.action: Inspect and upgrade surge protection devices in the DC field to prevent damage from electrical surges.
actions.expected_impact: Enhanced surge protection can lower the risk of fire incidents, which are responsible for 24.7% of the equipment cost and have recurred within 90 days.

actions.action: Establish a cleaning schedule for modules to reduce dirt accumulation, especially under conditions of 'ciel dégagé' and 'vent modéré'.
actions.expected_impact: Regular cleaning can decrease the likelihood of severe incidents, which account for 15.5% of the equipment cost and have a recurrence within 90 days.

actions.action: Perform fire-risk inspections focusing on support structures and PV panels, especially during calm weather conditions.
actions.expected_impact: Proactive inspections can prevent fire incidents, which have no severe incidents but account for 4.7% of the cost and have recurred once.

actions.action: Maintain a stock of critical spare parts for the inverter and DC connectors to enable quick corrective actions.
actions.expected_impact: Availability of spare parts can reduce downtime and mitigate the impact of failures related to inverter performance.
